tasks.title: Concurrent cell prepares keep invalidating each other's readiness validation
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). Seen 2026-10-31 on Portswood Rec (53,-42) with neighbour sessions preparing 52,-42/52,-43: `prepare --apply` on one cell changed the readiness revision of neighbouring cells, so a separate prepare then apply was refused 'validation stale' four times; builders had to chain prepare && apply in one shell command. Revision = content_id([POLICY, facts revision, plan_identity]) in lib/journal/cell_readiness.py; I did not find which input changes (suspect vector-map extract rewrite or neighbour plan notes). Questions: should validation of cell A depend on neighbour state at all? Should apply refresh validation itself under the lock? Decide, then fix.

tasks.title: prepare --apply records a duplicate plan_feature on every run (ambiguous legacy plan warning)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. On 53,-42 repeated `prepare --apply` added a second plan `houses_brickfield_road` for the same 6 houses already planned as houses_brickfield_road_w176633174, with warning 'ambiguous legacy plan ... no readable handoff spec'; a duplicate `houses_kitchener_road` (bare id from the 2026-10-29 build in row -43) also showed planned in 53,-42. I dismissed both with dismiss-feature. Decide whether prepare should skip groups already covered by a spec-backed plan, and how legacy bare ids should be matched.

tasks.title: Feature builds across a cell edge silently invalidate a finished neighbour and may generate ghost cells
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (policy). Applying houses_kitchener_road_w176634502 (footprint z -5382..-5343) reached 5 blocks into finished cell 53,-43 and marked its trees/decor stale (trees=False, decor=False). An earlier apply also generated a lidar ghost cell at 56,-40 (230k blocks, 'ghost-ground' journal seq 620) that the user did not ask for. Decide: warn/confirm before an apply touches a done neighbour; keep or drop frontier ghost generation on feature applies; whether edge fringe (roof overhang) should invalidate trees/decor at all.

tasks.title: reapply_feature refuses legacy house builds with no recorded builder; house_build apply bypasses the guard
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. houses_kitchener_road_w176658416 could not be reapplied (reapply_feature: no available recorded builder). At the owner's request I applied its old spec directly with house_build.py --apply under the lock (31905 positions, 0 mismatches), which bypasses the legacy-builder refusal and still leaves no recorded builder. Decide whether to backfill builder records for legacy spec-backed features (links #225, #228) so reapply works, and whether direct spec apply should be allowed for them.

tasks.title: World provider osm_extract.py: ogr2ogr ran without OSM_CONFIG_FILE; duplicates lib/sources
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. In worlds/southampton-build/providers/geofabrik-hampshire/osm_extract.py run_ogr2ogr passed no --config OSM_CONFIG_FILE, so GDAL 3.13's default schema (no `amenity` on points) failed the furniture preset and blocked `prepare --apply`. I patched it in the world checkout (osm_config(): world downloads/osmconf.ini else TOOL_ROOT/config/osmconf.ini); the patch is uncommitted and has no test, on top of the owner's existing uncommitted edits. The world provider duplicates the presets and run_ogr2ogr in lib/sources/geofabrik_provider.py; decide whether to delete the copy and call the tool one. Also: manifest hints from prepare (`ref_manifest.py add ...` for prepared-53--42 and prepared-54--42, 52,-42, 52,-43) were not run.

tasks.title: Sparse front boundaries in cell 53,-43 (Kitchener and Sirdar roads): walls, fences, hedges and gates
tasks.notes:
Owner review 2026-11-08 of 53,-43 (southampton-build): very little decor outside house fronts. Not measured yet. Related: #240 (shared frontage between ground and decor), snag S-073. Start by measuring decor per frontage against the aerial and street-run convention, then decide whether the cause is the decor layer or missing boundary evidence. Needs a live world to verify. Spun out of #243 (doors, closed).

DIAGNOSIS 2026-11-09 (read-only; decor report highfield_53_m43_decor-report.json + garden_sources.garden_barriers report).
Measure: 59 eligible fronts in the cell (Kitchener 31, Sirdar 28). 26 have no decor at all. 186 of 1,981 front-yard columns carry decor (~9%), all aerial-hedge fragments. Zero walls, fences or gates; zero furniture in the whole cell (furniture 0). Frontage `boundary` is empty on all 59. Sparse is true on both streets equally.
Aerial (reference/aerial/kitchener-z19 mosaic): fronts are not plain. Most have a low pale wall on the pavement line, side dividing walls or hedges, a paved drive or path gap, gravel/lawn with shrubs, some bins.
Where lost: (1) EVIDENCE, the main cause. A front boundary needs a `front` spec in site/gardens/<street>.json or an aerial hedge (hedge_share >= 0.6). kitchener_road.json has only rear/side vetoes, no `front`; sirdar_road.json does not exist. Aerial hedge fired on 12 of 59 front segments; low walls read pale, not green, so the detector cannot see them. (2) Aerial-hedge fronts never feed residential_frontage `boundary`/`opening` (role_spec only), so those hedges get no entrance gap from the opening logic (route columns are still reserved). (3) No source for private-yard furniture: only map furniture and reference/decor-furniture.json (no 53,-43 entry). (4) NOT the cause: layer drops inside fronts are 29 columns (22 against build, 5 above lidar, 2 blocked); route+clearance take 5-11 columns of 14-58 per yard.
Proposed fix: (a) world data, no code: add `front` (low wall, height 1) and `side_front` to kitchener_road.json and a new sirdar_road.json, citing a registered aerial evidence id; per-house `front: none` where the aerial shows an open drive. (b) code, garden_sources.residential_frontage / garden_barriers: pass the resolved front spec (convention or aerial hedge) into the frontage so `boundary` and `opening` are set for aerial hedges too; widen the opening to the drive width where the route meets a paved strip. Tests in lib/sources/test_garden_sources.py: aerial-hedge front gets an opening; convention front wall leaves the route open. (c) owner decision first: whether to add a front-yard furniture convention (bins beside the opening, planters), labelled inference.
Verify: per-front table before/after (decor columns in extent, boundary length, opening present), decor dry run on 53,-43, then an in-world look along both roads.

OWNER DECISION 2026-11-09: a front yard here should have walls, hedges, fences, bushes, ideally flowers, sheds, garages, ponds and gates. Every element still needs aerial or map evidence per property; nothing is scattered by default. Owning layer for each element: walls, fences, hedges, gates = decor (this task: front/side_front conventions, aerial hedge -> boundary and opening, gate block in the opening; gates are not built today, the opening is left as air). Bushes = trees (bush_voxels for small crowns; check whether front-yard shrubs show in the canopy mask or are lost). Flowers = ground foliage (foliage.py flower list; check whether guessed lawn in private frontage gets any). Sheds and garages = outbuildings: cell_features.py leaves them 'to their house plot' and coverage.py lists OUTBUILDINGS, but nothing appears to build them; this is a gap of its own. Ponds = only mapped natural=water polygons become water_body features; garden ponds from the aerial have no source. Split 2026-11-09 (owner agreed): this task keeps walls, fences, hedges and gates. Sheds and garages moved to #251; bushes, flowers and garden ponds moved to #252. RE-SCOPED 2026-11-10 (docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md): part (a) of the diagnosis, boundary evidence per street, overlaps #255 (district vibe profile); the aerial-hedge opening gap overlaps #240's open item; street furniture is now #260. Blocked by #255. What remains here: the live measurement and the in-world verification against the aerial.

[Review 2026-11-12] Rebuilt 53,-43 ground then decor after #240/#245-247: doors, boundary openings (419 reserved) and routes hold; road-facing fronts still show no boundary (decor = 150 aerial hedge items + 2 mapped iron bars; 79 of 143 frontages ineligible 'no street-run frontage evidence'). Owner confirmed in-world (snag S-077 on I-042). Part (a) of the proposed fix is world data only (front/side_front in kitchener_road.json, new sirdar_road.json, citing a registered aerial evidence id and the owner's Street View for S-073) and needs no code, so it can be done before #255 if the owner wants it sooner; the aerial-hedge opening gap (b) waits on #254. The pavement/forecourt split is tracked on #254, the material fallback on #255.

[Rebuild gate 2026-11-12, owner] Do not rebuild 53,-43 ground or decor to judge this until every task that changes how it builds has landed: #253, #254, #255 (class table, wiring, district profile with material fallback), #252 (bushes, flowers, ponds in front gardens) and #260 (street furniture), plus this task's own boundary data. An earlier rebuild repeats effort and shows the same result. Not gating: #249 (audit tool only); #251 and #261 are already done. Judge snag S-077 (I-042) only after that rebuild.

[#252 research 2026-11-12] Planting measured on 53,-43: front gardens have 0 flowers and 0 bushes (59 eligible plots, 1,981 frontage columns), no garden water on the aerial. Bushes and flowers need labelled inference rules, now tasks #265 and #266 (blocked by #253, #254); they add to the rebuild gate. Ponds need no task.

[Research 2026-11-12, docs/plans/244-boundary-evidence-findings.md] Decisions per street run with evidence ids, 7 Kitchener and 13 Sirdar houses read open (front: none), draft data in docs/plans/244-draft/ (kitchener_road.json, sirdar_road.json). Correction: Street View (67 Kitchener Rd) shows weathered timber fence about 1 m, not low pale wall; only 68-62 and 48-46 read as low wall on the aerial. Part (a) data is now task 267 (blocked by 268, the evidence registration); it needs no code and may land before #255 if the owner confirms the Sirdar inference. Drive-width opening is task 270. The existing side_front: none vetoes on 33-51, 55, 59 look too broad. Not decided: material from above, whether open forecourts have a low wall, any gates; Sirdar has no street view. Note (2026-11-14): owner decision recorded in docs/plans/244-boundary-evidence-findings.md: side_front is open by default (supersedes the earlier 'keep front side dividers' draft and the #267 vetoes).

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Street furniture: labelled lamp and bench inference where the map has no points (I-008)
tasks.notes:
Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md section 4. I-008: the vector-map cache for 48,-44 held no point features on 2026-10-27, so benches, bins, bike racks, lamp posts and bollards had no source. lib/sources/street_furniture.py already defines the kinds, recipes and extract presets. A candidate cause is #237 (the furniture preset failed under GDAL's default schema, world provider patch uncommitted); that is blocked on the owner and is not part of this task. Deliver the inference only: labelled street lamps along roads at a spacing set by OSM highway class (residential, tertiary and above, footway), benches at a low density on paths in park and leisure land (#253 classes), kept off door routes, entrance openings and carriageways, never reported as observed; a mapped point or designer trace wins. Spacing comes from the district profile (#255) when present, else a default per highway class. Whether OSM lit tags are available is unverified: use them when present, state when absent. This direction (2026-11-10) supersedes #244's 'nothing scattered by default' for street furniture only. Blocked by #254 because both change decor_plan and decor_layer. Files: lib/sources/street_furniture.py, lib/layers/decor_plan.py, decor_layer.py and their tests. Check: unit tests on synthetic road strips (spacing per highway class, door-route clearance, labelled inference, mapped point wins) via python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only <stem>; a dry-run decor report for one built cell shows furniture counts by provenance; no live apply. World review (separate, owner): rebuild decor in one cell and judge street feel.

[Design 2026-11-11, docs/plans/land-use-classes.md] Lamp spacing comes from land_use.resolve: the district profile when present, else the top-level highways map in config/land-use-classes.json (owned by this task). Benches are inferred only where the adjoining class row has a furniture section, which ships for park only. Preferred order is after #255, but #254 alone is enough to start. Tests: plan section 8. TIGHTENED 2026-11-14, but the riskiest of the small tasks: it needs design judgement (spacing, door-route clearance, merging with mapped points) and touches decor_plan.py and decor_layer.py, which #265/#266 do not, so it can run alongside them. For a smaller model, do it in these steps and stop for review after step 2: (1) add pure functions in lib/sources/street_furniture.py: `lamp_positions(road_polyline, highway_class, spacing_table, rng_seed)` and `bench_positions(path_polyline, ...)` returning labelled items (kind, x, z, provenance source inference, confidence low) with tests on synthetic strips; (2) wire them into decor_plan behind the existing 'a mapped point or designer trace wins' rule and the door-route/opening/carriageway keep-out (reuse the existing reserved sets in decor_plan.plan items), with tests; stop and report. (3) only after review, a dry-run decor report counts by provenance for 53,-43. For a smaller model, do it in steps and stop for review after step 2: (1) add pure functions in lib/sources/street_furniture.py: `lamp_positions(road_polyline, highway_class, spacing_table, rng_seed)` and `bench_positions(path_polyline, ...)` returning labelled items (kind, x, z, provenance source inference, confidence low), with tests on synthetic strips; (2) wire them into decor_plan behind the 'a mapped point or designer trace wins' rule and the door-route/opening/carriageway keep-out (reuse the reserved sets decor_plan already builds), with tests; stop and report. (3) only after review, a dry-run decor report of counts by provenance for 53,-43.

tasks.title: A clear: line never names a command that cannot work for that plan
tasks.notes:
Found 2026-11-15 following #284's clear: line for cell 48,-44: 'recovery: mismatched apply west_w34391673 -> ... reconcile 48,-44 --fix ...; if it reports still mismatched, python3 scripts/reapply_feature.py --world <world> west_w34391673 --apply'. The reapply was then refused at preflight: 'no replayable recorded builder; see the unrecorded listing from scripts/builder_audit.py (#248), or use redo (redesign from evidence)'. So the sanctioned clearing command named was dead for this plan. (#287 later cleared this case by treating door open/powered as play state.)
Wanted: every clear: line names only commands that can work for that plan now. For a mismatched feature apply, check whether the plan has a replayable recorded builder (the same check reapply_feature's preflight uses) and name reapply only if it does; otherwise name the redo route (redo skill / redo_layer or feature redo command, whichever is sanctioned) and say why reapply is not offered. Same audit for the other clear: lines added in #284/#285: a test per blocker kind that the named command's own preflight would accept the case.
Files: lib/journal/cell_readiness.py (clear_with), the reconcile 'still mismatched' message in scripts/cell_registry.py, tests. Not a stretch.
